questions.prompt: One question took 3 model requests before the text answer. How many turns and steps is that?
questions.explanation: A turn answers one user message, so this is 1 turn. Each model request inside it is a step, so it has 3 steps.

questions.prompt: A task must read 12 files, one per step, and then answer. What happens with a step limit of 10?
options: The loop stops before the answer, because the task needs at least 13 steps
It works, because tool results do not count as steps
The model reads all 12 files in step 1
The program raises the limit by itself
questions.explanation: Each file takes one step and the answer takes one more, so the task needs 13 steps. A limit of 10 stops it halfway.

questions.prompt: Why does the program count the steps instead of trusting the model to stop?
options: The model can only count to 10
The API charges a fee for each turn
Steps are free, so the count is only for logs
The model often cannot tell that it repeats itself, and each step costs more tokens
questions.explanation: A stuck model may ask for the same tool again and again. Each step resends a longer conversation, so the program must cap the steps.
